_comment: Screener engine config. Read-only fundamental screening of Indian stocks via the vendored screener-india port. THIS ENGINE NEVER PLACES AN ORDER.
_doc: See Blue_engine/screener/README.md. Every key below is optional; the code defaults match these values.

_source_help: source='sector'  -> sweep sector tables (fast, ~1 request per 50 names)
source='symbols' -> fetch one company page per symbol (slow, most accurate)
source='screen'  -> read a saved public screen on screener.in
screener._symbols_help: Used when source='symbols'. These two are the acceptance smoke test.
screener._sectors_help: Used when source='sector'. Slugs come from client.list_sectors(). NIFTY-500-ish root is IN02.
screener._screen_help: Used when source='screen'. Find ids with list_screens() in the dashboard or the CLI.
screener._caps_help: Polite limits. The scraper is bounded on purpose - see polite_limits() in the engine output.
screener._enrich_help: Per-symbol company-page fetch to fill metrics missing from the sector table. Off by default (it multiplies request count by N).
screener._transport_help: min_interval_ms is twice the upstream npm default (200ms). Raise it if you ever see HTTP 429.
screener._auth_help: Only needed for PRIVATE saved screens, and only a limited capability. 'sessionid=<value>' copied from a logged-in browser session.

screen.name: mktcap200_de_lt1
screen._rules_help: TWO requested rules. Strict inequalities: exactly 200 Cr or exactly D/E 1.0 is EXCLUDED.
_on_missing_help: fail    -> metric missing means the name is EXCLUDED (default, safest)
unknown -> excluded, but tagged as a data problem rather than a violation
pass    -> the rule is ignored for this name (use with care)
screen._exclude_sectors_help: Banks/NBFCs/insurers report debt/equity that is not a solvency measure (borrowings ARE their inventory). Excluded from the debt rule by default.
screen._exclude_symbols_help: Hard block list, applied before any rule.

_example_provider_use._comment: The pure pipeline path: hand Alpha a pre-built universe instead of scraping. The screener engine accepts the same shape via context['screener_inputs'] or a provider_ref.
